target: Διάβαζα όταν ήρθε η Μαρία.
english: I was reading when Maria came.
tip: The ongoing past sets the scene, the one-off past interrupts: διάβαζα (diávaza = I was reading) when ήρθε (írthe = came) cuts in.

target: Έβλεπα τηλεόραση και ξαφνικά χτύπησε η πόρτα.
english: I was watching TV and suddenly there was a knock at the door.
tip: ξαφνικά (xafniká = suddenly) is a signal word – it flips the sentence to the one-off past: χτύπησε (chtýpise = it knocked), not the ongoing form.

target: Παλιά κάπνιζε πολύ, αλλά πέρσι σταμάτησε.
english: He used to smoke a lot, but last year he stopped.
tip: Habit vs change: κάπνιζε (he used to smoke), σταμάτησε (stamátise = he stopped, once).

target: Δεν άκουσα το τηλέφωνο γιατί άκουγα μουσική.
english: I didn't hear the phone because I was listening to music.
tip: Same verb, two pasts: άκουσα = I heard (once), άκουγα (ákouga) = I was listening.

target: Ήθελα να έρθω, αλλά δεν μπόρεσα.
english: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
tip: Wanting is a state, managing is one-off: ήθελα, αλλά δεν μπόρεσα (íthela, allá den bóresa).

target: Περίμενα μισή ώρα και μετά έφυγα.
english: I waited half an hour and then I left.
tip: περίμενα μισή ώρα (perímena misí óra) can mean 'I waited' or 'I was waiting' half an hour – the two past forms coincide here, so context decides.

target: Μιλούσαμε για σένα όταν μπήκες!
english: We were talking about you when you walked in!
tip: για usually means 'for', but after speech verbs it's 'about': μιλούσαμε για σένα (miloúsame gia séna = we were talking about you).

target: Έκανε κρύο, αλλά βγήκαμε βόλτα.
english: It was cold, but we went out for a walk.
tip: Background weather takes the ongoing past: έκανε κρύο (ékane krýo = it was cold); the one-off event gets the simple past – βγήκαμε (vgíkame = we went out).

target: Όταν δούλευα εκεί, ξυπνούσα στις πέντε.
english: When I worked there, I used to wake up at five.
tip: Two habits, two imperfects: δούλευα... ξυπνούσα (doúleva... xypnoúsa).

target: Έγραφα ένα μέιλ όταν χτύπησε το τηλέφωνο.
english: I was writing an email when the phone rang.
tip: χτυπάω for phones and doors: χτύπησε το τηλέφωνο (chtýpise = it rang).

target: Ενώ μαγείρευα, ήρθαν οι φίλοι μας.
english: While I was cooking, our friends arrived.
tip: ενώ + imperfect = while: ενώ μαγείρευα (enó mageíreva = while I was cooking).

target: Μόλις μπήκα, κατάλαβα ότι κάτι έγινε.
english: As soon as I walked in, I realized something had happened.
tip: μόλις + aorist = as soon as: μόλις μπήκα (mólis bíka = as soon as I came in).

target: Αύριο θα ξυπνήσω στις έξι.
english: Tomorrow I'll wake up at six.
tip: θα + one-shot form = a single future act: θα ξυπνήσω (tha ksipníso = I'll wake up).

target: Θα περάσω από την τράπεζα το μεσημέρι.
english: I'll stop by the bank at midday.
tip: θα περάσω από την τράπεζα (tha peráso apó tin trápeza) – lit. 'I'll pass from the bank': περνάω από (pernáo apó) is how you say stop by.

target: Θα γυρίσω σπίτι κατά τις οχτώ.
english: I'll get home around eight.
tip: κατά τις οχτώ (katá tis ochtó = around eight) — κατά makes a time approximate.

target: Απόψε θα κοιμηθώ νωρίς.
english: Tonight I'll go to sleep early.
tip: θα κοιμηθώ (tha kimithó = I'll sleep) – the ending looks passive, but this verb has no other shape: sleeping just comes in passive form.

target: Δεν θα βγω απόψε, είμαι κουρασμένος.
english: I won't go out tonight, I'm tired.
tip: δεν θα βγω (den tha vgo = I won't go out) – 'not' goes first, before the future word, never between it and the verb.

target: Θα σε πάρω τηλέφωνο το βράδυ.
english: I'll call you tonight.
tip: The object pronoun sits inside the future phrase: θα σε πάρω (tha se páro = I'll call you) – σε (se = you) slots between θα (tha) and the verb.

target: Θα σου πω τα νέα μου αύριο.
english: I'll tell you my news tomorrow.
tip: θα σου πω (tha su po = I'll tell you) – the little word for 'you' slips in between the future marker and the verb.

target: Θα σε περιμένω έξω από το σινεμά.
english: I'll wait for you outside the cinema.
tip: θα σε περιμένω (tha se periméno = I'll wait for you) – Greek drops the 'for': you wait someone, directly.

target: Θα τα πούμε σύντομα!
english: We'll talk soon!
tip: θα τα πούμε (tha ta púme = we'll talk, lit. we'll say them) — a standard goodbye.

target: Θα της ζητήσω συγγνώμη για χθες.
english: I'll apologize to her for yesterday.
tip: Greek asks for forgiveness rather than 'apologizing': θα της ζητήσω συγγνώμη (tha tis zitíso signómi = I'll ask her for forgiveness).

target: Θα μπορέσω να έρθω τελικά!
english: I'll be able to come after all!
tip: θα μπορέσω (tha boréso = I'll manage to) — one occasion, vs μπορώ in general.

target: Θα σου τηλεφωνήσω μόλις φτάσω.
english: I'll phone you as soon as I arrive.
tip: μόλις + future-type form = as soon as: μόλις φτάσω (mólis ftáso = as soon as I arrive).

target: Την Κυριακή θα φάμε στης μαμάς μου.
english: On Sunday we'll eat at my mom's.
tip: στης μαμάς (stis mamás = at mom's) — the word σπίτι is understood.

target: Την Κυριακή θα κοιμάμαι μέχρι αργά!
english: On Sunday I'll be sleeping in late!
tip: θα + present-type form = ongoing future: θα κοιμάμαι (tha kimáme = I'll be sleeping).

target: Θα σας κάνουμε τραπέζι το Σάββατο!
english: We'll have you over for dinner on Saturday!
tip: κάνω τραπέζι (káno trapézi = host a meal, lit. make a table) — an invitation to dinner.

target: Του χρόνου θα πάμε διακοπές στην Κρήτη.
english: Next year we'll go on vacation to Crete.
tip: του χρόνου (tu chrónu = next year, lit. of the year).

target: Θα κλείσω τα εισιτήρια απόψε.
english: I'll book the tickets tonight.
tip: κλείνω (klíno) literally means 'close' – Greek closes what it books: θα κλείσω τα εισιτήρια (tha klíso ta isitíria = I'll book the tickets). Tables too.

target: Θα κολυμπάμε κάθε πρωί στη θάλασσα.
english: We'll swim in the sea every morning.
tip: κάθε πρωί = repeated, so the future keeps the present-type form: θα κολυμπάμε (tha kolymbáme).
